attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own newsletter post, stated as fact.

semantics.note: The normalised proposition leaves out the claim that Altman moved Friar's reporting line as a reaction to her doubts. The contract keeps that claim. 'Observation' is the right kind.

contract.note: Reading 'margins' as 2025 gross margin against the earlier projection is a fair, ordinary reading. The speaker may have meant revised outlooks rather than realized results, and the contract's choice of 2025 and gross margin shapes the result.

evidence.note: Reporting, via The Information, that Friar privately doubted a late-2026 IPO. Supports the CFO-stance part only.
Fortune says Friar has reported to Simo since August 2025. That casts doubt on the change being a reaction to the recently reported doubts, but it does not date when the doubts began.
A secondary account of leaked slides: OpenAI's 2025 adjusted gross margin was 33% against a 46% target. Supports the OpenAI margin part only, and is not independently verified.
Anthropic's S-1 (available Oct 26) no longer presents gross profit, so it gives no matched comparison with the earlier projection.

reviews.rationale: Reporting backs the CFO-doubt part, and a secondary source backs the OpenAI margin shortfall. Nothing in the packet establishes Anthropic's realized-versus-projected margin. The claim that the reporting line changed in reaction to her doubts is unverified, and e2 (structure in place since Aug 2025) complicates it without disproving it. Neither the support condition nor the contradiction condition is fully met.

attribution.note: Zitron's own unqualified statement in his own post.

semantics.note: An unhedged claim that tokenmaxxing spend will be the first to go. The cost-cut circumstance comes from the adjacent heading, and the contract notes it. No deadline is given.

contract.note: The plain reading (withdrawn ahead of comparable discretionary spending when costs are cut) is fair and ordinary. The comparison group is the evaluator's choice.

evidence.note: Microsoft's internal limits on tokenmaxxing (Aug 2026). Shows a policy shift, not lost supplier revenue or the order of cuts.
Management says it is not optimizing for fewer tokens. Mentions Claude Code license cuts and Uber's budget overrun, but no comparative order of withdrawals.

reviews.rationale: No deadline was stated, and the early-resolution rule needs dated records showing tokenmaxxing spend withdrawn before comparable spending, with lost supplier receipts. The packet shows only isolated policy limits and one vendor switch, which the rule says are not enough.
